fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses “…because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.” That's the reason the passage gives, so I'll leave it right there. Two voices, one complaint, and it's already out in the open.
Close, but that's not the point, friend. Miriam and Aaron aren't saying the LORD has gone quiet. They ask, “Does He not also speak through us?” That's about Him speaking through them as well.

I wish it worked that way, friend. You know when you're venting about a coworker, you turn around, and they're standing right there? Here, the text says plainly, “And the LORD heard this.” So it didn't stay between the two of them.
That's it, friend. The LORD says to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” The text says He spoke suddenly. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies.
The Jordan isn't mentioned in this passage, baker. The LORD's words are, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” That's where the three go, and it's where He comes down to meet them.

True, friend. The LORD says, “But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.” He calls Moses His servant and says it right in front of Aaron and Miriam. That's a strong thing to hear the LORD say about you.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles…” That's how plainly He speaks with Moses. With me, a recipe that says 'bake until done' is about as clear as a riddle.

Yes, friend. Aaron turns, sees Miriam, and says to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.” He's speaking to the very one he and Miriam spoke against. That's a humbling moment.
Joshua is Moses' assistant (Numbers 11:28), but the passage doesn't mention him here. Aaron speaks to Moses, saying, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.”
Caleb, from the tribe of Judah (Numbers 13:6), isn't named in this scene, baker. Aaron's words go straight to Moses: “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.”
Right, friend. Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!” The one Miriam and Aaron criticized is the one who pleads for Miriam. Short, plain and straight from the heart.
Forty is a fair guess, friend, but here the LORD says, “Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days…” Seven is the number in this verse.
Yes, friend. The text says, “…the people did not move on until she was brought in again.” The whole camp waits for Miriam. They stay where they are until she's back.
